title: Linked List Frequency
statement:
`head` is the first node of a non-empty singly linked list of integers. For each distinct value in the list, find how many nodes carry that value.

Build and return a new linked list holding exactly these counts: one node per distinct value, so the new list is as long as the number of distinct values. The counts may be placed in any order.
notes:
## Intuition

Each output node is just a tally, so the task is a counting problem dressed up as a list problem. A brute-force idea is to copy the values into an array, sort it and measure each run of equal values. A hash map does the same job in one pass without sorting: walk the list, bump the tally of each value, then turn the tallies into a new list.

## Approach

1. Walk the list with `node` and add one to `count` for `node.val`.
2. Create a `dummy` node and let `tail` point at it; it marks where the next result node goes.
3. For each `frequency` stored in `count`, attach a new node holding it after `tail` and move `tail` onto it.
4. Return `dummy.next`, the first real node.

## Example 1, step by step

List `1 → 1 → 2 → 1 → 2 → 3`.

- The counting pass ends with `count = {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 1}` (a `Map` keeps first-seen order).
- Building: `tail` gains a node `3`, then `2`, then `1`.

The answer is `[3, 2, 1]`; any ordering of these counts is accepted.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count and one pass over at most n distinct values.
- Space: O(k) for the map and the k result nodes, where k is the number of distinct values.

## Pitfalls

- The result holds counts, not the values themselves; `[1, 2, 3]` for example 1 would be wrong even though it has the right length.
- Equal values need not be adjacent (`1, 2, 1`), so counting neighbouring runs without sorting first gives too many nodes.
- Forgetting to advance `tail` overwrites the same `next` link each time and leaves a one-node list.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | map from each value to the number of nodes holding it |
| `node` | cursor for the counting pass |
| `dummy` | placeholder node in front of the result list |
| `tail` | last node of the result built so far |
| `frequency` | one tally taken from `count` |

narration.2: count will map each value to how many nodes carry it.
narration.3: Visit every node of the input list once.
narration.4: Add one to the tally of this node's value.
narration.7: A dummy node gives the result list a fixed starting point.
narration.8: tail marks the last node of the result so far.
narration.9: Take each distinct value's tally in turn.
narration.10: Hang a new node holding the tally after tail.
narration.11: Move tail onto the new node so the next one goes after it.
